companyDescription: AI networking + custom silicon · guiding Q3 AI semiconductor revenue to ~$16B, more than 200% YoY — the arms dealer for hyperscaler custom accelerators
priceNote: Live price Aug 13 07:49, flat on the day (-0.01%) while the rest of AI semis ran 2-5% — which is why it is the only large-cap still inside its own entry zone. Prior report (Aug 10) used $425.10, so -2.1% drift.
summary: The numbers going into Q3 are unusually concrete for a company this size: Broadcom has guided Q3 FY2026 revenue to roughly $29.4B, up about 84% year-over-year, with AI semiconductor revenue guided to approximately $16.0B — more than 200% growth. Consensus sits at $518.66 across 41 analysts (32 Strong Buy, 3 Moderate Buy, 6 Hold), about +24.7% from $416.05. Corrects a date error in the prior report: results are Thursday Sep 3 after close, not Sep 2. The honest counterweight is that AVGO's own recent prints have not rewarded strength — it fell 12.6% after Jun 2026 and was flat (-0.6%) in Aug 2026 — so the setup is 'good company, exhausted reaction function', and buying 21 days ahead of the print is exactly what this dashboard's measured base rate argues against.

catalysts.name: Q3 FY2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Thursday Sep 3, 2026 after market close (corrected from Sep 2 in the prior report). Guided to ~$29.4B revenue (+84% YoY) with AI semis ~$16.0B (+200%+). The read that matters is whether custom-silicon order visibility extends into FY2027 rather than the headline beat.

catalysts.name: Google TPU / Custom Silicon Demand Trajectory
catalysts.description: Custom accelerator programs are the structural driver behind the AI revenue ramp. Continuous rather than dated — it shows up as backlog commentary and mix, not as an announcement.

risks: AVGO's reaction function has turned hostile to good news: -12.6% after the Jun 2026 print and -0.6% in Aug 2026. A beat is close to priced

Measured base rate on this dashboard is -6.9% median return from report price to just after the catalyst, with 74% of picks underwater at their own event (n=54) — buying 21 days ahead of a print is the specific behaviour that produces that number
The earnings_beat bucket is 0-for-42 on +30%/14d; the $518.66 consensus is a 12-month target, not a 21-day expectation
AI revenue guided +200% YoY sets a comparison base that becomes brutal in FY2027 — deceleration is the de-rating risk even if absolute numbers stay large
Hyperscaler customer concentration: a handful of buyers drive the custom-silicon ramp, and one re-sourcing decision resets the trajectory
At ~$1.97T this is a market-weight AI proxy — a hawkish Sep 16 FOMC or an AI-capex scare hits it with the index, not independently of it

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds 3.50-3.75%, held Jul 29 for a fifth straight meeting with three dissents preferring a hike. Next FOMC Sep 16, two weeks after the print.
macroRisk.inflationNote: July CPI (Aug 12) headline 3.4% from 3.5%, core 2.5%, +0.1% m/m — soft enough to cut hike odds, following July payrolls at -23k with >100k of downward revisions.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: AVGO is one of the largest single expressions of the AI capex trade. With the S&P at record highs and VIX near 14.9, positioning is the risk channel — a hawkish surprise hits crowded AI semis harder than the index, and AVGO is now a meaningful share of that index itself.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — earnings quality isn't the question; crowding and index concentration are.

entryStrategy.verdict: Best-quality setup on the board and the only large-cap still in its zone — but the measured base rate (-6.9% at-catalyst, 74% underwater) and a sub-2:1 R/R from $416 both say accumulate at $395-405 rather than buy the print at today's price.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Notably absent, which is the interesting part: AVGO was flat today (-0.01%) while NVDA +3.0%, MU +4.9% and MRVL +2.3% ran. The usual 1-2 week pre-earnings drift has not started, so unlike most of the board this pick is not being bought ahead of its own event. Feedback prior: earnings_beat is n=42 with medianExcessVsBenchPct +1.8 vs +1.4 overall — neither leader nor laggard, so no tier-2 adjustment.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 1-2 สัปดาห์ก่อนงบ (ยังไม่เริ่ม)

postWin.note: The range is the warning. NVDA gained 24% on a May 2023 print that reset estimates, but AVGO's own recent prints delivered -0.6% (Aug 2026) and -12.6% (Jun 2026) despite strong numbers. For a $1.97T company a beat alone is not a catalyst.

postLose.note: AVGO's own Jun 2026 print took it down 12.6%. That is the realistic downside on a guidance disappointment, and it is deeper than the -14% corpus median MAE suggests for a mega-cap.

spotSizing.reason: Core Holding sizing — business quality and 41-analyst coverage depth justify a larger position than the speculative names on this board. Not raised despite being the only large-cap in zone, because the entry rule says the preferred fill is $395-405, not today's price.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the measured -14% median MAE; a break here before Sep 3 means the AI capex narrative is cracking rather than AVGO specifically

stopPostCatalyst.note: On a guidance disappointment, trim rather than exit — the Jun 2026 -12.6% recovered, and this is a Core Holding
